proposal.name: Replay current bugs through command drivers

plan.name: Replay current bugs through command drivers
plan.summary: Execute every required current-bug TLC path in ordinary TypeScript, existing TypeScript and ordinary Python gates, including the factory's verify.Run path, independently of normal sampling and its budgets, while existing Python applications continue to refuse replay until their authenticated adapter exists. Supply separate gate-owned replay harnesses and a documented driver factory that initializes real code, binds each concrete action and typed argument list to an actual application method, reads its state and closes it; the harness invokes those methods, owns ordering and completion, and the shared replay contract checks the exact prefix and each forbidden operation, with no application changes, synthetic bug mutations or driver-authored successful observations. Preserve the ordinary commands, fixed random defaults, dependency images, selected-source hashes, no-network sandboxes, resource limits, streaming recording ownership, model/proof/build/tried-step/larger-bound checks and legacy drivers; make incomplete, stale, malformed or exceptional replay, process and cleanup failures fail closed, and keep sample counts separate from replay and forbidden terminal states. Retain independent per-bug evidence and stable JSON-round-trip fingerprints in reports, receipts and dashboard views, show the bug, offending operation and observed state on reproduction, make factory availability notices route-aware without hiding unsupported temporal replays, and update synthesis and read-only review guidance to inspect real operation bindings and read-back. Update SPEC.md with a citation to #913's ratified plan, docs/gate.md and docs/factory.md with the implemented interface and existing-Python limitation, and README.md's concise gate description within 400 lines; ship self-contained regressions for both #789 sequences on all three routes, including actual pinned TLC and runtime execution in the existing integration lane, with no workflow, decision-journal or ratified-lock edits and no deferred part of this step.

tests.name: TestCommandReplayFindsBothDeliveryBugs913
tests.says: All three command routes keep a passing sample that misses both delivery/reload/recovery bugs, then independently replay every current bug through verify.Run; either reproduced bug fails the gate and both corrected operations pass, without inflating sampled coverage or losing receipt fingerprints. The same self-contained fixtures must run with actual drivers, application methods, gate harnesses and pinned TLC/runtime images in an integration-tagged regression in the existing PR lane.

tests.name: TestCommandReplayRejectsIncompleteExecution913
tests.says: After proving healthy replay works, each route refuses a missing interface or second bug, skipped or altered prefixes, null dispatch, unexpected exceptions, malformed, duplicate, conflicting or stale evidence, nonzero processes, missing markers and failed cleanup; no other successful obligation can mask these failures.

tests.name: TestCommandReplayCancellationAndCompatibility913
tests.says: Fresh identities survive concurrent gate checks, canceling or timing out a running replay cannot pass or leak its storage, model-only and legacy gates do not execute replay, existing source import checks remain enforced and replay imports do not make sampling exhaustive.

tests.name: TestSynthesisAndReviewRequireRealReplayBindings913
tests.says: Synthesis supplies the separate replay interface and harness guidance on each supported route, and the read-only reviewer inspects the real application bindings, exact prefixes and read-back, without claiming exhaustive coverage or claiming existing Python replay support.

tests.name: TestFactoryReplayAvailabilityMatchesAdapters913
tests.says: Factory proposal and amendment availability reflects the three implemented adapters while existing Python and temporal obligations remain visibly unsupported.

tests.name: TestDashboardShowsCommandReplayDiagnostics913
tests.says: The dashboard retains independent model catches and per-bug replay status and diagnostics, including the offending operation and observed state, and does not warn that supported command adapters are unavailable.
